title: UK AI Bill 2026 — Regulatory Coordination and Sandbox Provisions
context: 2026-08-29 — UK Government published AI Bill white paper response; DSIT leading cross-regulator coordination via DRCF
body: The UK AI Bill 2026 introduces a statutory duty on UK regulators (ICO, FCA, CMA, Ofcom, MHRA) to coordinate AI oversight through the Digital Regulation Cooperation Forum (DRCF). Key provisions for AI system operators: (1) Mandatory registration of high-risk AI systems with the DRCF central registry by Q1 2027 — systems must carry a machine-readable compliance credential linked to measured benchmarks. (2) Regulatory sandboxes for AI must accept independently verified measurement evidence (Council of AI signed credentials qualify as admissible assessment findings under the sandbox fast-track provisions). (3) Cross-sector coordination means a single measurement credential can satisfy overlapping requirements across ICO (data protection), FCA (consumer duty), and Ofcom (online safety) — reducing duplication. (4) The Bill adopts an outcomes-based approach: operators must demonstrate measured containment, not just documented intent. The Council of AI 14-axis measurement board maps directly to DRCF sandbox evidence requirements for care, privacy, governance, and detector-interoperability axes.
